chapter_text:
CHAPTER 15 — हिमालयो नाम नगाधिराजः (HIMALAYO NAMA NAGADHIRAJAH)

Introduction — प्रस्तावना

No mountain on earth has inspired a literature as vast and as loving as the Himalaya has inspired in Sanskrit. From the Vedas and the epics to the court poetry of Kalidasa, the Himalaya (हिम + आलयः = 'the abode of snow') appears again and again as the guardian of India's north, the father of the goddess Parvati, the home of gods and sages, and the source of the great rivers that feed the plains. In this lesson (NIOS Senior Secondary Sanskrit, Course 309) we study the most celebrated of all Himalayan verses — the opening श्लोक of Kalidasa's महाकाव्य 'कुमारसम्भवम्' — together with its शब्दार्थ, अन्वय and poetic beauty; we then read original Sanskrit prose describing the mountain's geography, rivers, forests, wildlife and pilgrimage sites; and finally we draw grammar from the chapter: सन्धि, समास (especially तत्पुरुष and बहुव्रीहि in the mountain's epithets), विभक्ति and कृदन्त forms.

The opening verse of Kumarasambhava — कुमारसम्भवस्य प्रथमः श्लोकः

Kalidasa's Kumarasambhava narrates the story that leads to the birth of Kumara (Kartikeya), son of Shiva and Parvati. Since Parvati is the daughter of the mountain (पर्वतस्य पुत्री पार्वती), the poem fittingly begins with a majestic portrait of her father, the Himalaya:

अस्त्युत्तरस्यां दिशि देवतात्मा हिमालयो नाम नगाधिराजः ।
पूर्वापरौ तोयनिधी वगाह्य स्थितः पृथिव्या इव मानदण्डः ॥ (कुमारसम्भवम् 1.1)

शब्दार्थ (word meanings): अस्ति = there is; उत्तरस्यां दिशि = in the northern direction; देवतात्मा = divine-souled, whose very self is divine (देवता आत्मा यस्य सः — बहुव्रीहि); हिमालयः नाम = Himalaya by name; नगाधिराजः = the overlord/king of mountains (नगानाम् अधिराजः); पूर्वापरौ = the eastern and the western (two); तोयनिधी = the two oceans (तोयानां निधी, 'treasuries of water', द्विवचन); अवगाह्य (वगाह्य) = having plunged into, having entered; स्थितः = stands, is situated; पृथिव्याः = of the earth; इव = as if, like; मानदण्डः = a measuring rod.

अन्वय (prose order): उत्तरस्यां दिशि देवतात्मा हिमालयः नाम नगाधिराजः अस्ति। (सः) पूर्वापरौ तोयनिधी अवगाह्य पृथिव्याः मानदण्डः इव स्थितः (अस्ति)।

Translation: In the northern direction there stands the divine-souled king of mountains named Himalaya who, dipping into the eastern and the western oceans, stands like the measuring rod of the earth.

Poetic appreciation — the मानदण्ड image: Kalidasa is famed above all for his similes — 'उपमा कालिदासस्य' says the old verse. Here, in a single उपमा, the poet makes the reader see the whole subcontinent at once: the mountain range stretches from the western sea to the eastern sea like a golden rod laid across the top of India, as if some cosmic surveyor had set down a scale (मानदण्डः) to measure the greatness of the earth. The image suggests three things together: (1) immensity — only something spanning ocean to ocean could 'measure' the earth; (2) dignity — a मानदण्ड is a standard, and the Himalaya is the standard by which all mountains (and all greatness) are measured; (3) divinity — the mountain is देवतात्मा, not mere rock but a living divine being, a fitting father for the goddess Parvati. In the very first verse the उपमेय (the thing described) is the Himalaya and the उपमान (the thing compared to) is the measuring rod, joined by the word इव.

A second verse of Kalidasa on the Himalaya (कुमारसम्भवम् 1.3):

अनन्तरत्नप्रभवस्य यस्य हिमं न सौभाग्यविलोपि जातम् ।
एको हि दोषो गुणसन्निपाते निमज्जतीन्दोः किरणेष्विवाङ्कः ॥

Meaning: Of that (Himalaya), the source of countless gems, the snow never became a destroyer of its splendour; for a single fault sinks (unnoticed) in a multitude of virtues, as the dark spot of the moon (sinks) in its rays. Here Kalidasa answers an imagined objection — is not endless snow a defect? No, he says: where virtues are heaped together, one flaw disappears, just as we forget the moon's dark mark in the beauty of its light. This is a सुन्दर अर्थान्तरन्यास (corroboration by a general truth) joined to an उपमा.

The Himalaya in the Bhagavadgita: In the Vibhuti-yoga the Lord himself counts the Himalaya among his own glories — 'स्थावराणां हिमालयः' (भगवद्गीता 10.25) — 'Among the immovable things I am the Himalaya.' Thus scripture and poetry alike treat the mountain as the very presence of the divine on earth.

हिमालयस्य वर्णनम् — Original Sanskrit prose with English

हिमालयः भारतस्य उत्तरस्यां दिशि प्रहरीव तिष्ठति। सः शीतलान् उत्तरवातान् निवारयति, मेघान् च अवरुध्य वृष्टिं कारयति। अतः एव भारतभूमिः सस्यश्यामला वर्तते। (The Himalaya stands like a sentinel in India's north. It wards off the cold northern winds and, blocking the clouds, causes the rains — therefore the land of India is green with crops.)

अस्मात् नगाधिराजात् गङ्गा यमुना ब्रह्मपुत्रः सिन्धुः इत्यादयः महानद्यः प्रभवन्ति। गङ्गा गङ्गोत्रीहिमानीतः गोमुखात् भागीरथीरूपेण निःसरति, यमुना च यमुनोत्रीतः। एताः नद्यः कोटिशः जनान् जीवयन्ति, क्षेत्राणि सिञ्चन्ति, अतः जनाः ताः मातृवत् पूजयन्ति। (From this king of mountains rise the great rivers — Ganga, Yamuna, Brahmaputra, Sindhu and others. The Ganga issues from the Gangotri glacier at Gomukh in the form of the Bhagirathi, and the Yamuna from Yamunotri. These rivers give life to crores of people and water the fields; hence people revere them like mothers.)

हिमालयस्य वनेषु देवदारुभूर्जादयः वृक्षाः शोभन्ते, महौषधयश्च प्रभवन्ति। तत्र कस्तूरीमृगः हिमचित्रकः (हिमव्याघ्रः) मोनाल-पक्षी च निवसन्ति। उत्तराखण्डे 'पुष्पघाटी' (Valley of Flowers) इति प्रसिद्धा उपत्यका वर्तते। (In the Himalayan forests shine the deodar, the birch and other trees, and great medicinal herbs grow. There live the musk deer, the snow leopard and the monal bird. In Uttarakhand lies the famous Valley of Flowers.)

हिमालयः तपोभूमिः तीर्थभूमिश्च अस्ति। गङ्गोत्री यमुनोत्री केदारनाथः बदरीनाथः इति चत्वारि धामानि तत्र विराजन्ते। केदारनाथः शिवस्य, बदरीनाथः च विष्णोः क्षेत्रम्। अमरनाथगुहायां हिममयं शिवलिङ्गं दृश्यते। ऋषयः मुनयश्च पुरा हिमालये एव तपः आचरन्। अतः कवयः तं भारतस्य मुकुटम् इति वदन्ति। (The Himalaya is a land of austerity and pilgrimage. The four shrines — Gangotri, Yamunotri, Kedarnath and Badrinath — stand there. Kedarnath is Shiva's seat, Badrinath is Vishnu's. In the Amarnath cave an ice linga of Shiva is seen. Sages of old performed their tapas in the Himalaya itself; hence the poets call it the crown of India.)

Geography at a glance: The Himalayan chain runs roughly 2,400 kilometres from west to east across the north of the Indian subcontinent. Its highest summit is Everest (in Nepal, called सगरमाथा in Nepali); the highest peak within India is Kanchenjunga. Poets read the range's east-west sweep as touching the Bay of Bengal and the Arabian Sea — the पूर्वापरौ तोयनिधी of Kalidasa's verse — a poetic, not literal, geography that captures how the mountain spans the whole breadth of the land. Beyond the main range lie Kailash and Lake Mansarovar, goals of the hardiest pilgrims.

व्याकरणम् — Grammar from the chapter

(A) सन्धि (Sandhi). • अस्ति + उत्तरस्याम् → अस्त्युत्तरस्यां: the इ of अस्ति meets उ and becomes य् — यण्-सन्धि (इ/ई + dissimilar vowel → य्). • हिम + आलयः → हिमालयः and नग + अधिराजः → नगाधिराजः: like vowels merge into one long vowel — सवर्णदीर्घ-सन्धि (अ + आ = आ; अ + अ = आ). • देवता + आत्मा → देवतात्मा (आ + आ = आ, दीर्घ). • पृथिव्याः + इव → पृथिव्या इव: the visarga is dropped before a vowel — विसर्ग-सन्धि. • तोयनिधी + अवगाह्य → तोयनिधी वगाह्य: in the verse the initial अ of अवगाह्य merges with the preceding long ई; restore it in the अन्वय as अवगाह्य. Being able to split these (सन्धि-विच्छेद) is essential for reading kavya.

(B) समास (Compounds) — the epithets of the mountain are a textbook of compounds. • हिमालयः = हिमस्य आलयः 'the abode of snow' — षष्ठी-तत्पुरुषः. • नगाधिराजः = नगानाम् अधिराजः 'the overlord of mountains' — षष्ठी-तत्पुरुषः. • देवतात्मा = देवता आत्मा यस्य सः 'he whose self is divine' — बहुव्रीहिः; the compound does not mean 'the soul of the gods' but points OUTSIDE itself to the Himalaya, the possessor — the defining mark of a बहुव्रीहि. • तोयनिधी = तोयानां निधी 'treasuries of water' (the oceans) — षष्ठी-तत्पुरुषः, here in the dual. • पूर्वापरौ = पूर्वश्च अपरश्च 'the eastern and the western' — द्वन्द्वः. • मानदण्डः = मानस्य दण्डः 'rod of measuring' — षष्ठी-तत्पुरुषः. • तपोभूमिः = तपसः भूमिः; तीर्थभूमिः = तीर्थानां भूमिः — both तत्पुरुष.

(C) कृदन्त (Primary derivatives). • अवगाह्य 'having plunged into' — the ल्यप् (gerund) form used because the root has the prefix अव (compare क्त्वा in simple roots: गत्वा, कृत्वा). • स्थितः 'standing, situated' — the क्त (past participle) of स्था, agreeing with नगाधिराजः in gender, number and case.

(D) विभक्ति (Cases in the verse). • उत्तरस्यां दिशि — सप्तमी (locative): 'in the northern direction'. • पूर्वापरौ तोयनिधी — द्वितीया द्विवचन (accusative dual), objects of अवगाह्य. • पृथिव्याः — षष्ठी (genitive): 'of the earth'. • हिमालयः, नगाधिराजः, देवतात्मा, स्थितः, मानदण्डः — all प्रथमा (nominative), describing the subject.

SUMMARY (सारांश)

In this chapter you studied the Himalaya as Sanskrit literature sees it: the divine-souled king of mountains. You learned Kalidasa's opening verse of the Kumarasambhava with its शब्दार्थ, अन्वय and translation, and appreciated the famous मानदण्ड simile — the mountain as the measuring rod of the earth, spanning ocean to ocean. You read how a single flaw drowns in a flood of virtues (1.3), and how the Gita names the Himalaya among the Lord's glories (स्थावराणां हिमालयः). Through original Sanskrit prose you surveyed the mountain's geography — guardian of the north, maker of rains, source of the Ganga (from Gangotri/Gomukh) and Yamuna (from Yamunotri) — its deodar and birch forests, musk deer and snow leopard, and its holy places: the four dhams, Amarnath and Kailash-Mansarovar. Finally you drew grammar from the text: यण्, दीर्घ and विसर्ग सन्धि; तत्पुरुष, बहुव्रीहि and द्वन्द्व समास in the mountain's epithets; the ल्यप् form अवगाह्य and the क्त form स्थितः; and the cases of the key words of the verse. The Himalaya, the poets say, is the crown of India — भारतस्य मुकुटम्.

sections.heading: Why the Kumarasambhava opens with the Himalaya
bullets: The Kumarasambhava tells the story leading to the birth of Kumara (Kartikeya), son of Shiva and Parvati; Parvati is पर्वतस्य पुत्री, the daughter of the mountain, so the poem begins with her father's portrait.
The Himalaya is देवतात्मा — divine-souled — not mere rock but a living divine being; the Gita too counts it among the Lord's glories: स्थावराणां हिमालयः.
From the Vedas and epics to court poetry, the Himalaya appears as guardian of the north, home of gods and sages, and father of rivers.

sections.heading: The verse: text, anvaya and translation
bullets: Text: अस्त्युत्तरस्यां दिशि देवतात्मा हिमालयो नाम नगाधिराजः। पूर्वापरौ तोयनिधी वगाह्य स्थितः पृथिव्या इव मानदण्डः॥
अन्वय: उत्तरस्यां दिशि देवतात्मा हिमालयः नाम नगाधिराजः अस्ति; सः पूर्वापरौ तोयनिधी अवगाह्य पृथिव्याः मानदण्डः इव स्थितः।
Translation: In the north stands the divine-souled king of mountains named Himalaya who, dipping into the eastern and western oceans, stands like the measuring rod of the earth.
Key words: नगाधिराजः = overlord of mountains; तोयनिधी = the two oceans (dual); अवगाह्य = having plunged into; मानदण्डः = measuring rod.

sections.heading: The manadanda simile and verse 1.3
bullets: उपमेय: the Himalaya; उपमान: the measuring rod (मानदण्डः); comparison word: इव — a classic उपमा from the poet of whom it is said 'उपमा कालिदासस्य'.
The image conveys immensity (spanning ocean to ocean), dignity (the standard by which greatness is measured) and divinity (देवतात्मा).
Verse 1.3 answers the objection that endless snow is a flaw: one दोष sinks in a heap of गुण, as the moon's dark spot disappears in its rays (अनन्तरत्नप्रभवस्य यस्य...).
The Himalaya is called the source of countless gems and great herbs (अनन्तरत्नप्रभवः, महौषधयः).

sections.heading: Geography, rivers, forests and wildlife
bullets: The chain runs roughly 2,400 km across the north; it wards off the cold northern winds and blocks the monsoon clouds, causing the rains that keep India green.
The Ganga rises from the Gangotri glacier at Gomukh as the Bhagirathi; the Yamuna rises at Yamunotri; the Brahmaputra and Sindhu are also Himalayan-born.
Everest is the highest summit; Kanchenjunga is the highest peak within India; the verse's ocean-to-ocean sweep (पूर्वापरौ तोयनिधी) is poetic geography.
Forests of deodar (देवदारु) and birch (भूर्ज) shelter the musk deer (कस्तूरीमृगः), the snow leopard and the monal; Uttarakhand's Valley of Flowers is world-famous.

sections.heading: Pilgrimage, tapas and the chapter's grammar
bullets: The four dhams — Gangotri, Yamunotri, Kedarnath (Shiva) and Badrinath (Vishnu) — plus Amarnath's ice linga and Kailash-Mansarovar make the Himalaya India's great तीर्थभूमि; the rishis chose it as their तपोभूमि.
सन्धि: अस्ति + उत्तरस्याम् = अस्त्युत्तरस्यां (यण्); हिम + आलयः = हिमालयः (सवर्णदीर्घ); पृथिव्याः + इव = पृथिव्या इव (विसर्ग lost).
समास: हिमालयः and नगाधिराजः are षष्ठी-तत्पुरुष; देवतात्मा is बहुव्रीहि (देवता आत्मा यस्य सः); पूर्वापरौ is द्वन्द्व.
कृदन्त: अवगाह्य is the ल्यप् gerund (prefix अव + गाह्); स्थितः is the क्त participle of स्था; उत्तरस्यां दिशि is सप्तमी, पृथिव्याः is षष्ठी.

key_takeaways: Kumarasambhava 1.1 introduces the Himalaya as देवतात्मा नगाधिराजः — the divine-souled king of mountains — standing in the north like the earth's measuring rod (मानदण्डः).
The मानदण्ड simile joins immensity, dignity and divinity in one image; उपमेय is the Himalaya, उपमान the rod, इव the comparison word.
Verse 1.3 teaches that one flaw drowns in many virtues — the moon's spot is forgotten in its light; the Himalaya's snow never dims its splendour.
The Himalaya guards India from cold winds, causes the rains, and gives birth to the Ganga (Gangotri/Gomukh), the Yamuna (Yamunotri) and other great rivers.
It is India's तीर्थभूमि and तपोभूमि — the four dhams, Amarnath and Kailash — and shelters deodar forests, musk deer, snow leopard and monal.
हिमालयः and नगाधिराजः are षष्ठी-तत्पुरुष compounds; देवतात्मा is a बहुव्रीहि pointing to the possessor, not the parts.
अस्त्युत्तरस्यां shows यण्-सन्धि (इ + उ = यु); अवगाह्य is a ल्यप् gerund and स्थितः a क्त participle.

glossary.definition: The overlord/king of mountains (नगानाम् अधिराजः, षष्ठी-तत्पुरुष); Kalidasa's title for the Himalaya.
'Whose self is divine' — a बहुव्रीहि compound (देवता आत्मा यस्य सः) describing the Himalaya as a living divine being.
A measuring rod or standard of measure; in the simile, the Himalaya laid across the north is the earth's measuring rod.
'Treasury of water' — the ocean (तोयानां निधिः); the dual तोयनिधी in the verse means the eastern and western oceans.
'Having plunged into' — the ल्यप् (gerund) form of अव + गाह्; appears in the verse as वगाह्य by sandhi.
The simile, Kalidasa's signature figure of speech, comparing an उपमेय to an उपमान with a word like इव.
The subject being described in a simile — here the Himalaya; the standard of comparison is the उपमान (the measuring rod).
Kalidasa's mahakavya on the events leading to the birth of Kumara (Kartikeya), son of Shiva and Parvati; it opens with the Himalaya.
A great mass of snow, a glacier; the Ganga rises from the Gangotri glacier (गङ्गोत्रीहिमानी) at Gomukh.
A land of austerity (तपसः भूमिः); the Himalaya, where the rishis of old performed their tapas.
A holy place of pilgrimage; the Himalayan tirthas include the four dhams, Amarnath and Kailash-Mansarovar.
The deodar tree ('wood of the gods'), the great cedar of the Himalayan forests.
The musk deer of the high Himalaya, source of the fragrant kasturi (musk).
A compound whose meaning points outside its own parts to a possessor, e.g. देवतात्मा = he WHOSE self is divine.
The sandhi in which इ/ई, उ/ऊ, ऋ before a dissimilar vowel become य्, व्, र् — e.g. अस्ति + उत्तरस्याम् = अस्त्युत्तरस्यां.

worksheet.title: Worksheet — हिमालयो नाम नगाधिराजः (NIOS Sanskrit 309, Chapter 15)
worksheet.instructions: Attempt all questions. Write Sanskrit in Devanagari and explanations in English. Quote the verse where asked and show sandhi and samasa working step by step.

questions.question: 'अस्त्युत्तरस्यां दिशि देवतात्मा...' — this verse opens which mahakavya?
questions.explanation: It is the first verse of Kalidasa's Kumarasambhava.

questions.question: In the verse, the Himalaya is said to stand like the earth's
questions.explanation: पृथिव्या इव मानदण्डः — like the measuring rod of the earth.

questions.question: True or False: देवतात्मा is a बहुव्रीहि compound meaning 'he whose self is divine'.
questions.explanation: देवता आत्मा यस्य सः — the compound points to the possessor, the mark of a बहुव्रीहि.

questions.question: Complete the verse: पूर्वापरौ तोयनिधी वगाह्य स्थितः पृथिव्या इव ____ ।
questions.explanation: The verse ends पृथिव्या इव मानदण्डः.

questions.question: Write the अन्वय (prose order) of Kumarasambhava 1.1 and translate it into English.
questions.answer: अन्वय: उत्तरस्यां दिशि देवतात्मा हिमालयः नाम नगाधिराजः अस्ति। (सः) पूर्वापरौ तोयनिधी अवगाह्य पृथिव्याः मानदण्डः इव स्थितः। Translation: In the northern direction there is the divine-souled king of mountains named Himalaya; plunging into the eastern and western oceans, he stands like the measuring rod of the earth.
questions.explanation: The anvaya restores natural prose order and the full form अवगाह्य.

questions.question: Do the सन्धि-विच्छेद (split) and name the sandhi: (a) अस्त्युत्तरस्यां (b) हिमालयः.
questions.answer: (a) अस्त्युत्तरस्यां = अस्ति + उत्तरस्याम् — यण्-सन्धि (the इ before उ becomes य्). (b) हिमालयः = हिम + आलयः — सवर्णदीर्घ-सन्धि (अ + आ = आ).
questions.explanation: Both splits come straight from the chapter's grammar section.

questions.question: Name the sources of the Ganga and the Yamuna, and state one way the Himalaya protects India.
questions.answer: The Ganga rises from the Gangotri glacier at Gomukh (flowing first as the Bhagirathi); the Yamuna rises at Yamunotri. The Himalaya protects India by walling off the cold northern winds (and by blocking the monsoon clouds it causes the rains).
questions.explanation: Geography facts from the chapter's prose description.

questions.question: Read the passage and answer: 'हिमालयः तपोभूमिः तीर्थभूमिश्च अस्ति। गङ्गोत्री यमुनोत्री केदारनाथः बदरीनाथः इति चत्वारि धामानि तत्र विराजन्ते। केदारनाथः शिवस्य, बदरीनाथः च विष्णोः क्षेत्रम्।' — (a) Which four dhams are named? (b) Whose shrine is Kedarnath and whose is Badrinath?
questions.answer: (a) The four dhams named are Gangotri, Yamunotri, Kedarnath and Badrinath. (b) Kedarnath is the shrine (क्षेत्रम्) of Shiva, and Badrinath is the shrine of Vishnu.
questions.explanation: Direct comprehension of the chapter's Sanskrit prose on the Himalayan tirthas.

questions.question: Appreciate the simile 'पृथिव्या इव मानदण्डः'. Identify the उपमेय, उपमान and comparison word, and explain what the image conveys about the Himalaya.
questions.answer: In this उपमा the उपमेय (subject described) is the Himalaya, the उपमान (standard of comparison) is the मानदण्ड or measuring rod, and the comparison word is इव. The image makes the reader see the whole subcontinent at once: the range stretches from the western sea to the eastern sea like a surveyor's rod laid across the top of India. It conveys three things together: immensity — only something spanning ocean to ocean could 'measure' the earth; dignity — a मानदण्ड is a standard, and the Himalaya is the standard by which all greatness is measured; and divinity — the rod belongs to a mountain already called देवतात्मा, divine-souled. This economy of suggestion is why tradition says 'उपमा कालिदासस्य' — the simile belongs to Kalidasa.
questions.explanation: Full appreciation: identify the parts of the simile and unfold its three suggestions.

questions.question: 'हिमालयः भारतस्य मुकुटम्' — justify this statement in an essay covering the mountain's geography, rivers, natural wealth and spiritual significance.
questions.answer: The Himalaya deserves to be called the crown of India on every count. Geographically it stands at the head of the land, a roughly 2,400 km wall across the north that wards off the freezing northern winds and blocks the monsoon clouds so that the rains fall and the plains stay green (सस्यश्यामला). As the father of rivers it sends down the Ganga from the Gangotri glacier, the Yamuna from Yamunotri, and the Brahmaputra and Sindhu besides — rivers revered as mothers because they water the fields and sustain crores of lives. Its natural wealth is unmatched: deodar and birch forests, great medicinal herbs, and rare creatures like the musk deer, snow leopard and monal. Spiritually it is India's तपोभूमि and तीर्थभूमि — the four dhams, Amarnath's ice linga and Kailash-Mansarovar draw pilgrims, and the rishis of old chose its silence for tapas. Kalidasa crowned it in poetry as देवतात्मा नगाधिराजः, and the Gita counts it among the Lord's own glories (स्थावराणां हिमालयः). A crown sits at the head, gleams with jewels and marks sovereignty — the Himalaya does all three for India.
questions.explanation: An evaluative essay drawing together geography, rivers, flora-fauna and spirituality.

questions.question: Who composed the mahakavya कुमारसम्भवम्?
questions.explanation: Kumarasambhava is one of Kalidasa's two mahakavyas (with Raghuvamsha).

questions.question: The verse 'अस्त्युत्तरस्यां दिशि देवतात्मा...' is the opening verse of
questions.explanation: It is Kumarasambhava 1.1, the very first verse of the poem.

questions.question: The Kumarasambhava narrates the events leading to the birth of
questions.explanation: कुमारसम्भवम् = 'the birth of Kumara', son of Shiva and Parvati.

questions.question: Why does the Kumarasambhava fittingly OPEN with a portrait of the Himalaya?
options: because the poet was born there
because Parvati, the heroine, is the daughter of the mountain
because the Ganga is the heroine
questions.answer: because Parvati, the heroine, is the daughter of the mountain
questions.explanation: पर्वतस्य पुत्री पार्वती — the poem begins with the heroine's father.

questions.question: In the Bhagavadgita (10.25) the Lord says: 'Among immovable things I am the ____'.
questions.explanation: स्थावराणां हिमालयः — from the Vibhuti-yoga.

questions.question: Kalidasa is traditionally famed as the master of which figure of speech?
questions.explanation: The old saying runs 'उपमा कालिदासस्य' — the simile belongs to Kalidasa.

questions.question: The name हिमालयः literally means
questions.explanation: हिम (snow) + आलयः (abode) = the abode of snow.

questions.question: Kumarasambhava 1.1 belongs to which सर्ग (canto) of the poem?
questions.explanation: 1.1 = first verse of the first canto.

questions.question: In Sanskrit tradition the Himalaya is treated as
options: a mere heap of rock and ice
a living divine being and father of Parvati
questions.answer: a living divine being and father of Parvati
questions.explanation: He is देवतात्मा, a person of the poem — Parvati's father and host of gods and sages.

questions.question: Complete the verse: अस्त्युत्तरस्यां दिशि ____ हिमालयो नाम नगाधिराजः।
questions.explanation: अस्त्युत्तरस्यां दिशि देवतात्मा हिमालयो नाम नगाधिराजः।

questions.question: Complete: हिमालयो नाम ____ ।
questions.explanation: हिमालयो नाम नगाधिराजः — the king of mountains named Himalaya.

questions.question: Complete: पूर्वापरौ ____ वगाह्य स्थितः...
questions.explanation: पूर्वापरौ तोयनिधी वगाह्य — plunging into the eastern and western oceans.

questions.question: The verse ends: स्थितः पृथिव्या इव ____ ।
questions.explanation: पृथिव्या इव मानदण्डः — like the measuring rod of the earth.

questions.question: According to the verse, the Himalaya stands in which direction?
questions.explanation: अस्त्युत्तरस्यां दिशि — in the northern direction.

questions.question: The form तोयनिधी in the verse is in which grammatical number?
questions.explanation: तोयनिधी is accusative dual — the TWO oceans, eastern and western.

questions.question: Which is the correct अन्वय of the second half of the verse?
options: (सः) पूर्वापरौ तोयनिधी अवगाह्य पृथिव्याः मानदण्डः इव स्थितः
पृथिवी तोयनिधी अवगाह्य मानदण्डम् इव स्थिता
मानदण्डः पृथिव्याः तोयनिधी इव अवगाह्य स्थितः
तोयनिधी पूर्वापरौ पृथिव्याम् इव मानदण्डे स्थितौ
questions.answer: (सः) पूर्वापरौ तोयनिधी अवगाह्य पृथिव्याः मानदण्डः इव स्थितः
questions.explanation: The Himalaya (सः) is the subject: having plunged into the two oceans, he stands like the earth's measuring rod.

questions.question: Which word in the verse means 'ocean'?
questions.explanation: तोयनिधिः = 'treasury of water', i.e. the ocean.

questions.question: अवगाह्य (वगाह्य) in the verse means
questions.explanation: अव + गाह् + ल्यप् = having plunged/dipped into (the oceans).

questions.question: The epithet देवतात्मा describes the Himalaya as
options: divine-souled — whose very self is divine
questions.answer: divine-souled — whose very self is divine
questions.explanation: देवता आत्मा यस्य सः — the mountain is a living divine being.

questions.question: मानदण्डः literally means
questions.explanation: मानस्य दण्डः — the rod used for measuring.

questions.question: The figure of speech in 'पृथिव्या इव मानदण्डः' is
questions.explanation: The word इव ('like') marks an explicit simile.

questions.question: In the simile of verse 1.1, the उपमेय (subject described) is
questions.explanation: The Himalaya is described; the मानदण्ड is the उपमान (standard of comparison).

questions.question: The मानदण्ड image suggests all of the following EXCEPT
options: the immensity of a range spanning ocean to ocean
the Himalaya as the standard by which greatness is measured
the fragility and impermanence of the mountain
questions.answer: the fragility and impermanence of the mountain
questions.explanation: The image conveys immensity, dignity and divinity — not fragility.

questions.question: In Kumarasambhava 1.3, a single fault amid many virtues is compared to
options: the dark spot of the moon sinking in its rays
questions.answer: the dark spot of the moon sinking in its rays
questions.explanation: निमज्जतीन्दोः किरणेष्विवाङ्कः — the moon's mark disappears in its light.

questions.question: In verse 1.3 the Himalaya is called अनन्तरत्नप्रभवः, meaning
questions.explanation: अनन्त (countless) + रत्न (gems) + प्रभवः (source).

questions.question: According to verse 1.3, the snow (हिमम्) of the Himalaya
questions.explanation: हिमं न सौभाग्यविलोपि जातम् — the snow never became a destroyer of its glory.

questions.question: The general truth stated in 1.3 — 'एको हि दोषो गुणसन्निपाते निमज्जति' — means
options: a single fault sinks unnoticed in a heap of virtues
questions.answer: a single fault sinks unnoticed in a heap of virtues
questions.explanation: Where virtues crowd together, one flaw disappears from view.

questions.question: शब्दार्थ: 'नगः' means
questions.explanation: नग = mountain ('that which does not move'); hence नगाधिराजः, king of mountains.

questions.question: शब्दार्थ: 'तोयम्' means
questions.explanation: तोय = water; तोयनिधिः = treasury of water = ocean.

questions.question: शब्दार्थ: 'निधिः' means
questions.explanation: निधि = treasure-store; the ocean is the store of waters.

questions.question: शब्दार्थ: 'पृथिवी' means
questions.explanation: पृथिवी = the earth; पृथिव्याः = 'of the earth' (genitive).

questions.question: शब्दार्थ: 'दिशि' (as in उत्तरस्यां दिशि) means
questions.explanation: दिश् = direction; दिशि is its locative — 'in the direction'.

questions.question: शब्दार्थ: 'हिमम्' means
questions.explanation: हिम = snow, frost; the first member of हिमालयः.

questions.question: शब्दार्थ: 'आलयः' means
questions.explanation: आलय = abode; हिमालयः = abode of snow.

questions.question: शब्दार्थ: 'अधिराजः' means
questions.explanation: अधि + राजन् = king over others; नगाधिराजः = overlord of mountains.

questions.question: शब्दार्थ: 'प्रहरी' (as in प्रहरीव तिष्ठति) means
questions.explanation: प्रहरी = guard, watchman; the Himalaya stands like a sentinel of India.

questions.question: शब्दार्थ: 'हिमानी' means
questions.explanation: हिमानी = a great mass of snow; गङ्गोत्रीहिमानी = the Gangotri glacier.

questions.question: शब्दार्थ: 'देवदारु' is
questions.explanation: देवदारु = 'wood of the gods', the deodar cedar of Himalayan forests.

questions.question: शब्दार्थ: 'कस्तूरीमृगः' is
questions.explanation: कस्तूरी (musk) + मृगः (deer) — the musk deer of the high Himalaya.

questions.question: शब्दार्थ: 'महौषधिः' means
questions.explanation: महा + औषधि = great herb; the Himalaya is famed for its medicinal plants.

questions.question: शब्दार्थ: 'तीर्थम्' means
questions.explanation: तीर्थ = sacred ford/pilgrimage place; the Himalaya is तीर्थभूमिः.

questions.question: The Ganga rises from which glacier?
questions.explanation: The Ganga issues from the Gangotri glacier at Gomukh.

questions.question: The Yamuna rises at
questions.explanation: Yamunotri in Uttarakhand is the source of the Yamuna.

questions.question: The highest summit of the Himalaya (and the world) is
questions.explanation: Everest, in Nepal (called Sagarmatha there), is the world's highest peak.

questions.question: The highest Himalayan peak lying within India is
questions.explanation: Kanchenjunga, on the Sikkim-Nepal border, is India's highest peak.

questions.question: The Himalayan chain stretches across India's north for roughly
questions.explanation: The range runs about 2,400 kilometres from west to east.

questions.question: One protective role of the Himalaya mentioned in the chapter is that it
options: wards off the cold northern winds
questions.answer: wards off the cold northern winds
questions.explanation: सः शीतलान् उत्तरवातान् निवारयति — it wards off the cold north winds.

questions.question: How does the Himalaya help cause the rains over India?
options: by melting its snow into clouds
by blocking the monsoon clouds so they shed rain
questions.answer: by blocking the monsoon clouds so they shed rain
questions.explanation: मेघान् अवरुध्य वृष्टिं कारयति — obstructing the clouds, it makes the rain fall.

questions.question: The Ganga's initial Himalayan stream, flowing from Gomukh, is called the

questions.question: Which set names rivers that are Himalayan-born?
questions.explanation: These rise in the Himalayan/trans-Himalayan region; the others are peninsular rivers.

questions.question: Relative to India, the Himalaya lies to the
questions.explanation: It walls the entire northern frontier of the subcontinent.

questions.question: The verse's पूर्वापरौ तोयनिधी are best read on the map of India as
options: the Bay of Bengal and the Arabian Sea (poetically)
questions.answer: the Bay of Bengal and the Arabian Sea (poetically)
questions.explanation: The east-west sweep touching two seas is poetic, not literal, geography.

questions.question: Why does the chapter say India is सस्यश्यामला (green with crops) thanks to the Himalaya?
options: because its snows keep the plains cold
because its rains and rivers water the fields
because its forests cover the plains
questions.answer: because its rains and rivers water the fields
questions.explanation: The mountain causes the rains and sends down the rivers that irrigate the land.

questions.question: Which group correctly lists the four Himalayan dhams of Uttarakhand?
questions.explanation: These four shrines form the Himalayan Char Dham of Uttarakhand.

questions.question: Kedarnath is a shrine of which deity?
questions.explanation: केदारनाथः शिवस्य क्षेत्रम् — Kedarnath is Shiva's seat.

questions.question: Badrinath is sacred to

questions.explanation: अमरनाथगुहायां हिममयं शिवलिङ्गं दृश्यते — a linga formed of ice.

questions.question: The name देवदारु for the Himalayan cedar literally suggests
questions.explanation: देव (god) + दारु (wood/timber).

questions.question: The musk deer of the Himalaya is prized for its
questions.explanation: The कस्तूरीमृग carries the famed fragrant musk.

questions.question: Why did the rishis of old choose the Himalaya for their tapas?
options: for its solitude, purity and sacred atmosphere
questions.answer: for its solitude, purity and sacred atmosphere
questions.explanation: As तपोभूमि, its stillness and sanctity suited meditation and austerity.

questions.question: The famous 'Valley of Flowers' (पुष्पघाटी) lies in which Indian state?
questions.explanation: The Valley of Flowers is a Himalayan valley in Uttarakhand.

questions.question: Mount Kailash and Lake Mansarovar, goals of the hardiest pilgrims, lie
options: beyond the main Himalayan range (in the Tibetan region)
at the source of the Yamuna
questions.answer: beyond the main Himalayan range (in the Tibetan region)
questions.explanation: Kailash-Mansarovar lies in the trans-Himalayan Tibetan region.

questions.question: हिमालयः = हिमस्य आलयः — this is which समास?
questions.explanation: The first member stands in the genitive relation: 'abode OF snow'.

questions.question: The विग्रह of नगाधिराजः is
questions.explanation: 'Overlord of mountains' — genitive tatpurusha.

questions.question: देवतात्मा (देवता आत्मा यस्य सः) is which समास?
questions.explanation: The compound denotes the possessor ('he WHOSE self is divine'), the mark of a bahuvrihi.

questions.question: अस्त्युत्तरस्यां = अस्ति + उत्तरस्याम् shows which सन्धि?
questions.explanation: इ before the dissimilar vowel उ becomes य् — yan sandhi.

questions.question: हिम + आलयः = हिमालयः shows which सन्धि?
questions.explanation: अ + आ merge into the single long आ — savarnadirgha sandhi.

questions.question: अवगाह्य ('having plunged into') is which kind of form?
options: a ल्यप् (gerund) of a prefixed root
a क्त्वा gerund of a simple root
questions.answer: a ल्यप् (gerund) of a prefixed root
questions.explanation: With the prefix अव, the gerund takes ल्यप् (-य), not क्त्वा.

questions.question: स्थितः in the verse is
questions.explanation: स्था + क्त = स्थितः 'standing/situated', agreeing with नगाधिराजः.

questions.question: उत्तरस्यां दिशि is in which विभक्ति?
questions.explanation: 'IN the northern direction' — locative of place.

questions.question: पूर्वापरौ (पूर्वश्च अपरश्च) is which समास?
questions.explanation: 'The eastern AND the western' — a dvandva (copulative) compound in the dual.

questions.question: Choose the correct translation of Kumarasambhava 1.1.
options: In the north stands the divine-souled king of mountains, Himalaya, who, dipping into the eastern and western oceans, stands like the earth's measuring rod.
In the south lies a great forest named Himalaya, which touches two rivers like a staff of gold.
The king of the north conquered the mountains and measured the earth with a rod.
The two oceans plunged into the Himalaya, which lay like a rod upon the earth.
questions.answer: In the north stands the divine-souled king of mountains, Himalaya, who, dipping into the eastern and western oceans, stands like the earth's measuring rod.
questions.explanation: This follows the anvaya faithfully: subject Himalaya, gerund अवगाह्य, simile मानदण्डः इव.

questions.question: Translate: 'स्थावराणां हिमालयः' (गीता 10.25).
options: Among the immovable things, I am the Himalaya.
The Himalaya moves among the mountains.
The Himalaya belongs to the gods.
questions.answer: Among the immovable things, I am the Himalaya.
questions.explanation: स्थावराणाम् = of/among immovable things; the Lord lists his glories.

questions.question: Translate: 'हिमालयात् गङ्गा प्रभवति'.
options: The Ganga rises from the Himalaya.
The Ganga flows into the Himalaya.
The Himalaya rises from the Ganga.
questions.answer: The Ganga rises from the Himalaya.
questions.explanation: हिमालयात् is ablative ('from the Himalaya'); प्रभवति = originates.

questions.question: Translate: 'हिमालयः भारतस्य मुकुटम् इव शोभते'.
options: The Himalaya shines like the crown of India.
India shines on the crown of the Himalaya.
The crown of India melts the Himalaya.
The Himalaya wears India as a crown.
questions.answer: The Himalaya shines like the crown of India.
questions.explanation: मुकुटम् इव = like a crown; शोभते = shines.

questions.question: True or False: The Kumarasambhava was composed by Kalidasa.
questions.explanation: It is one of Kalidasa's two mahakavyas.

questions.question: True or False: In the verse, the Himalaya is said to stand in the SOUTHERN direction.
questions.explanation: अस्त्युत्तरस्यां दिशि — it stands in the NORTHERN direction.

questions.question: True or False: The simile of verse 1.1 compares the Himalaya to a measuring rod of the earth.
questions.explanation: पृथिव्या इव मानदण्डः — like the earth's measuring rod.

questions.question: True or False: The word तोयनिधिः means 'a desert'.
questions.explanation: तोयनिधिः = 'treasury of water', i.e. the ocean.

questions.question: True or False: The Ganga rises at Yamunotri.
questions.explanation: The Ganga rises from the Gangotri glacier (Gomukh); Yamunotri is the Yamuna's source.

questions.question: True or False: The Himalaya shields India from the cold winds of the north.
questions.explanation: It stands like a sentinel, warding off the freezing northern winds.

questions.question: True or False: Kedarnath is a shrine of Vishnu.
questions.explanation: Kedarnath is Shiva's shrine; Badrinath is Vishnu's.

questions.question: True or False: The musk deer (कस्तूरीमृगः) is found in the Himalaya.
questions.explanation: The musk deer lives in the high Himalayan forests.

questions.question: True or False: देवतात्मा is a बहुव्रीहि compound because it denotes the possessor — 'he whose self is divine'.
questions.explanation: देवता आत्मा यस्य सः — the meaning points outside the compound to the Himalaya.

questions.question: True or False: The phrase 'स्थावराणां हिमालयः' occurs in the Bhagavadgita.
questions.explanation: It is from the Vibhuti-yoga, Gita 10.25.

questions.question: Complete the verse: अस्त्युत्तरस्यां दिशि ____ हिमालयो नाम नगाधिराजः।
questions.explanation: The Himalaya's first epithet in the verse is देवतात्मा, 'divine-souled'.

questions.question: Complete the verse: हिमालयो नाम ____ ।
questions.explanation: नगाधिराजः — 'the king of mountains' — completes the first line.

questions.question: Complete the verse: स्थितः पृथिव्या इव ____ ।
questions.explanation: The verse closes with the simile of the measuring rod, मानदण्डः.

questions.question: हिम + ____ = हिमालयः ('the abode of snow').
questions.explanation: हिम (snow) + आलयः (abode) with savarnadirgha sandhi.

questions.question: 'नग' इत्यस्य पर्यायपदं (synonym) लिखत: ____ ।
questions.explanation: नगः and पर्वतः both mean 'mountain'.

questions.question: 'तोयम्' इत्यस्य पर्यायपदं लिखत: ____ ।
questions.explanation: तोयम् and जलम् both mean 'water'.

questions.question: The Sanskrit word for 'the earth' used in the verse (in षष्ठी as पृथिव्याः) is ____ ।
questions.explanation: पृथिवी = the earth; its genitive singular is पृथिव्याः.

questions.question: गङ्गा ____-हिमानीतः गोमुखात् निःसरति। (name of the glacier)
questions.explanation: The Ganga issues from the Gangotri glacier at Gomukh.

questions.question: यमुना ____-तः निःसरति। (place of origin)
questions.explanation: The Yamuna rises at Yamunotri.

questions.question: भारतस्य उत्तरस्यां दिशि ____ प्रहरीव तिष्ठति।
questions.explanation: The Himalaya stands like a sentinel in India's north.

questions.question: केदारनाथः ____ देवस्य क्षेत्रम् अस्ति। (deity's name)
questions.explanation: Kedarnath is the shrine of Shiva.

questions.question: बदरीनाथः ____ क्षेत्रम् अस्ति। (deity's name in षष्ठी)
questions.explanation: Badrinath is the shrine of Vishnu (विष्णोः = 'of Vishnu').

questions.question: सन्धिं कुरुत: अस्ति + उत्तरस्याम् = ____ ।
questions.explanation: यण्-सन्धि: the इ becomes य् before उ.

questions.question: 'हिमस्य आलयः' इति विग्रहवाक्यस्य समासनाम ____ । (name the compound type)
questions.explanation: It is a षष्ठी-तत्पुरुष: 'abode OF snow'.

questions.question: अवगाह्य इति पदं ____-प्रत्ययान्तं कृदन्तरूपम् अस्ति। (name of the suffix)
questions.explanation: With the prefix अव, the gerund takes the ल्यप् suffix.

questions.question: Why does Kalidasa begin the Kumarasambhava — a poem about the birth of Kumara — with a description of the Himalaya?
questions.answer: The Kumarasambhava tells the story that leads to the birth of Kumara (Kartikeya), the son of Shiva and Parvati. Parvati is पर्वतस्य पुत्री — the daughter of the mountain Himalaya. Since the heroine's family must be introduced first, the poem fittingly opens with a majestic portrait of her father, the divine-souled king of mountains.
questions.explanation: The mountain is a character in the poem — Parvati's father — not mere scenery.

questions.question: Cite one verse each from Kalidasa and from the Bhagavadgita that glorifies the Himalaya, and state what each says.
questions.answer: Kalidasa: 'अस्त्युत्तरस्यां दिशि देवतात्मा हिमालयो नाम नगाधिराजः...' (कुमारसम्भवम् 1.1) — the Himalaya is the divine-souled king of mountains, standing like the earth's measuring rod. Bhagavadgita: 'स्थावराणां हिमालयः' (10.25) — among immovable things the Lord himself is the Himalaya.
questions.explanation: Both poetry and scripture treat the mountain as a divine presence.

questions.question: What does the epithet देवतात्मा tell us about how Sanskrit literature views the Himalaya, as opposed to seeing it merely as a mountain range?
questions.answer: देवतात्मा means 'he whose very self is divine'. The epithet shows that Sanskrit literature does not treat the Himalaya as a lifeless heap of rock and snow but as a living, divine person — the abode of the gods, the father of Parvati, a being worthy of reverence. This is why the mountain can act as a character in the Kumarasambhava and why pilgrims approach it as sacred ground.
questions.explanation: The bahuvrihi epithet personifies and deifies the mountain.

questions.question: Write Kumarasambhava 1.1 in full in Devanagari.
questions.answer: अस्त्युत्तरस्यां दिशि देवतात्मा हिमालयो नाम नगाधिराजः। पूर्वापरौ तोयनिधी वगाह्य स्थितः पृथिव्या इव मानदण्डः॥
questions.explanation: The opening verse of the first canto of the Kumarasambhava.

questions.question: Give the शब्दार्थ of: देवतात्मा, नगाधिराजः, तोयनिधी, अवगाह्य, मानदण्डः.
questions.answer: देवतात्मा = divine-souled, whose self is divine; नगाधिराजः = the overlord/king of mountains; तोयनिधी = the two oceans ('treasuries of water', dual); अवगाह्य = having plunged/dipped into; मानदण्डः = a measuring rod.
questions.explanation: The five key words of the verse.

questions.question: Write the अन्वय (prose word order) of Kumarasambhava 1.1.
questions.answer: उत्तरस्यां दिशि देवतात्मा हिमालयः नाम नगाधिराजः अस्ति। (सः) पूर्वापरौ तोयनिधी अवगाह्य पृथिव्याः मानदण्डः इव स्थितः (अस्ति)।
questions.explanation: The anvaya restores natural prose order and the full form अवगाह्य for वगाह्य.

questions.question: In the simile 'पृथिव्या इव मानदण्डः', identify the उपमेय, the उपमान and the comparison word.
questions.answer: उपमेय (the subject described) = the Himalaya; उपमान (the standard of comparison) = the मानदण्ड, the measuring rod; the comparison word (उपमावाचक) = इव ('like/as if').
questions.explanation: The three parts of an upama, from the most famous simile in Sanskrit poetry.

questions.question: State TWO ideas that the मानदण्ड (measuring rod) image conveys about the Himalaya.
questions.answer: (1) Immensity: only something stretching from the western ocean to the eastern ocean could serve to 'measure' the whole earth — the image makes us see the range spanning the entire breadth of the land. (2) Dignity/standard: a मानदण्ड is a standard of measurement, so the Himalaya is presented as the very standard by which all mountains — and all greatness — are measured.
questions.explanation: Immensity, dignity (and divinity, via देवतात्मा) are the suggestions of the image.

questions.question: Explain the idea of Kumarasambhava 1.3: how does Kalidasa answer the objection that the Himalaya's endless snow is a defect?
questions.answer: Kalidasa replies that the Himalaya is the source of countless gems (अनन्तरत्नप्रभवः), and its snow never became a destroyer of its splendour. He gives the general truth: a single fault sinks unnoticed where virtues are heaped together (एको हि दोषो गुणसन्निपाते निमज्जति), just as the moon's dark spot disappears in the beauty of its rays. One flaw amid many excellences simply does not count.
questions.explanation: An arthantaranyasa (corroborating general truth) joined to the moon simile.

questions.question: Give the शब्दार्थ (English meanings) of: नगः, तोयम्, निधिः, हिमानी, तीर्थम्.
questions.answer: नगः = mountain; तोयम् = water; निधिः = treasure/repository; हिमानी = a great mass of snow, a glacier; तीर्थम् = a holy place of pilgrimage.
questions.explanation: Core vocabulary of the chapter's verse and prose.

questions.question: Use each of these words in a short Sanskrit sentence of your own: हिमालयः, गङ्गा.
questions.answer: Examples: (1) हिमालयः भारतस्य उत्तरस्यां दिशि तिष्ठति। (The Himalaya stands in India's north.) (2) गङ्गा हिमालयात् प्रभवति। (The Ganga rises from the Himalaya.) Any grammatical sentences using the two words correctly are acceptable.
questions.explanation: Simple sentences testing active use of chapter vocabulary.

questions.question: Name four great rivers that rise in the Himalayan region, as listed in the chapter.
questions.answer: The Ganga, the Yamuna, the Brahmaputra and the Sindhu (Indus) — गङ्गा यमुना ब्रह्मपुत्रः सिन्धुः इत्यादयः महानद्यः.
questions.explanation: All four are Himalayan-born rivers named in the chapter's prose.

questions.question: Explain TWO ways in which the Himalaya protects and nourishes India.
questions.answer: (1) It stands like a sentinel (प्रहरी) in the north and wards off the cold northern winds, shielding the plains from freezing blasts. (2) It blocks the monsoon clouds, causing them to shed rain over India, and it sends down the great rivers (Ganga, Yamuna and others) that water the fields — keeping the land सस्यश्यामला, green with crops.
questions.explanation: Guardian against cold winds; maker of rains and mother of rivers.

questions.question: Where exactly does the Ganga begin its journey, and by what name does it first flow?
questions.answer: The Ganga begins at Gomukh, the snout of the Gangotri glacier (गङ्गोत्रीहिमानी) in Uttarakhand. It first flows under the name Bhagirathi (भागीरथी) before it becomes the Ganga.
questions.explanation: Gangotri glacier → Gomukh → Bhagirathi → Ganga.

questions.question: Kalidasa says the Himalaya dips into the eastern and western oceans (पूर्वापरौ तोयनिधी). Is this literally true on the map? How should a reader understand it?
questions.answer: Literally, the Himalayan range does not touch either sea — it ends well inland at both extremities. The statement is poetic geography: the roughly 2,400 km east-west sweep of the range spans the whole breadth of the northern subcontinent, so the poet imagines it stretching from the Bay of Bengal to the Arabian Sea. The exaggeration serves the मानदण्ड image — only an ocean-to-ocean rod could measure the earth.
questions.explanation: Poetic, not literal — a kavi-samaya serving the measuring-rod simile.

questions.question: Name the four Himalayan dhams and the deities of Kedarnath and Badrinath.
questions.answer: The four dhams are Gangotri, Yamunotri, Kedarnath and Badrinath. Kedarnath is the shrine of Shiva; Badrinath is the shrine of Vishnu.
questions.explanation: The Char Dham of the Uttarakhand Himalaya.

questions.question: Mention two trees and two animals of the Himalayan forests named in the chapter.
questions.answer: Trees: the deodar (देवदारु) and the birch (भूर्ज). Animals: the musk deer (कस्तूरीमृगः) and the snow leopard (हिमचित्रकः/हिमव्याघ्रः); the monal bird may also be mentioned.
questions.explanation: Flora and fauna from the chapter's prose description.

questions.question: Why is the Himalaya called both तपोभूमिः and तीर्थभूमिः? Explain each term with one example.
questions.answer: तपोभूमिः ('land of austerity') because the rishis of old performed their tapas there — its solitude, purity and sanctity suited meditation; the epics and kavyas picture sages' hermitages on its slopes. तीर्थभूमिः ('land of pilgrimage') because it holds India's great high shrines — e.g. the four dhams (Gangotri, Yamunotri, Kedarnath, Badrinath), the Amarnath cave with its ice linga, and Kailash-Mansarovar beyond the range.
questions.explanation: Austerity ground of the sages and pilgrimage ground of the people.

questions.question: Do the सन्धि-विच्छेद and name each sandhi: (a) अस्त्युत्तरस्यां (b) नगाधिराजः.
questions.answer: (a) अस्त्युत्तरस्यां = अस्ति + उत्तरस्याम् — यण्-सन्धिः (इ + उ → यु; the इ becomes य्). (b) नगाधिराजः = नग + अधिराजः — सवर्णदीर्घ-सन्धिः (अ + अ = आ).
questions.explanation: Both splits are worked in the chapter's grammar section.

questions.question: How do we know देवतात्मा is a बहुव्रीहि and not a तत्पुरुष? Give the विग्रह and explain.
questions.answer: विग्रह: देवता आत्मा यस्य सः — 'he WHOSE self is divine'. A तत्पुरुष would denote one of its own members (e.g. 'the self of the gods'), but देवतात्मा denotes neither देवता nor आत्मा; it points OUTSIDE the compound to a possessor — the Himalaya. This external reference (अन्यपदार्थप्रधानता) is the defining mark of a बहुव्रीहि.
questions.explanation: Bahuvrihi = the compound's sense rests on another word (the possessor).

questions.question: Translate into English: 'अस्मात् नगाधिराजात् गङ्गा यमुना इत्यादयः महानद्यः प्रभवन्ति। जनाः ताः मातृवत् पूजयन्ति।'
questions.answer: From this king of mountains rise the great rivers — the Ganga, the Yamuna and others. People revere them like mothers (मातृवत्).
questions.explanation: अस्मात् नगाधिराजात् is ablative — 'from this king of mountains'; मातृवत् = 'like a mother'.

questions.question: Translate into Sanskrit: 'The Himalaya stands in the northern direction of India.'
questions.answer: हिमालयः भारतस्य उत्तरस्यां दिशि तिष्ठति। (Also acceptable: भारतस्य उत्तरस्यां दिशि हिमालयः अस्ति।)
questions.explanation: उत्तरस्यां दिशि is locative; तिष्ठति/अस्ति both acceptable as the verb.

questions.question: Discuss the place of the Himalaya in Sanskrit literature and Indian life, citing Kalidasa's Kumarasambhava and the Bhagavadgita.
questions.answer: The Himalaya holds a place in Sanskrit literature that no other mountain holds in any literature. Kalidasa opens his Kumarasambhava with it: 'अस्त्युत्तरस्यां दिशि देवतात्मा हिमालयो नाम नगाधिराजः' — the divine-souled king of mountains, standing like the measuring rod of the earth (पृथिव्या इव मानदण्डः). The mountain is not scenery but a person of the poem: the father of Parvati, host of gods and sages. In verse 1.3 Kalidasa even defends it — its endless snow is no flaw, for one fault drowns in a heap of virtues as the moon's spot drowns in its rays. Scripture matches poetry: in the Gita's Vibhuti-yoga the Lord declares 'स्थावराणां हिमालयः' — among immovable things I am the Himalaya (10.25). In Indian life the mountain is equally central: it guards the north against the cold winds, causes the rains, and sends down the Ganga and Yamuna that feed the plains; its slopes hold the great tirthas — the four dhams, Amarnath, Kailash — and its silence made it the तपोभूमि of the rishis. Literature and life agree: the Himalaya is भारतस्य मुकुटम्, the crown of India.
questions.explanation: Weave together kavya, scripture, geography and pilgrimage into one evaluation.

questions.question: Write Kumarasambhava 1.1 in Devanagari, give its अन्वय, its शब्दार्थ (any six words) and a full English translation.
questions.answer: Verse: अस्त्युत्तरस्यां दिशि देवतात्मा हिमालयो नाम नगाधिराजः। पूर्वापरौ तोयनिधी वगाह्य स्थितः पृथिव्या इव मानदण्डः॥ अन्वय: उत्तरस्यां दिशि देवतात्मा हिमालयः नाम नगाधिराजः अस्ति; (सः) पूर्वापरौ तोयनिधी अवगाह्य पृथिव्याः मानदण्डः इव स्थितः। शब्दार्थ: उत्तरस्यां दिशि = in the northern direction; देवतात्मा = divine-souled; नगाधिराजः = king of mountains; तोयनिधी = the two oceans; अवगाह्य = having plunged into; मानदण्डः = measuring rod. Translation: In the northern direction there stands the divine-souled king of mountains named Himalaya who, dipping into the eastern and the western oceans, stands like the measuring rod of the earth.
questions.explanation: Full treatment of the verse: text, prose order, vocabulary and translation.

questions.question: 'उपमा कालिदासस्य' — appreciate the मानदण्ड simile of Kumarasambhava 1.1 in the light of this saying.
questions.answer: Tradition assigns each great poet his signature: the simile belongs to Kalidasa — उपमा कालिदासस्य. The opening of the Kumarasambhava shows why. In one image — पृथिव्या इव मानदण्डः — the poet makes the reader see the entire subcontinent from above: the mountain range laid across the top of India from the western sea to the eastern sea like a surveyor's golden rod. The simile's parts are perfectly fitted: the उपमेय is the Himalaya, the उपमान the measuring rod, joined by इव. And the image works on three levels at once. It conveys immensity — only a rod spanning ocean to ocean could measure the earth. It conveys dignity — a मानदण्ड is a standard, and the Himalaya is the standard by which all greatness is measured. It conveys divinity — this rod belongs to a being already named देवतात्मा, divine-souled, the fitting father of the goddess Parvati. No description by enumeration could achieve what this single comparison achieves in half a verse; such economy of suggestion is exactly what the old saying celebrates.
questions.explanation: A poetic-appreciation essay: parts of the simile plus its threefold suggestion.

questions.question: Give the शब्दार्थ of the following ten words and use ANY FOUR of them in Sanskrit sentences of your own: नगः, तोयम्, निधिः, आलयः, अधिराजः, प्रहरी, हिमानी, देवदारु, कस्तूरीमृगः, तीर्थम्.
questions.answer: शब्दार्थ: नगः = mountain; तोयम् = water; निधिः = treasure/repository; आलयः = abode; अधिराजः = overlord, supreme king; प्रहरी = sentinel/watchman; हिमानी = snow-mass, glacier; देवदारु = deodar (cedar) tree; कस्तूरीमृगः = musk deer; तीर्थम् = holy place of pilgrimage. Example sentences: (1) हिमालयः नगानाम् अधिराजः अस्ति। (2) हिमालयः भारतस्य प्रहरीव तिष्ठति। (3) वने देवदारवः शोभन्ते। (4) केदारनाथः प्रसिद्धं तीर्थम् अस्ति। Any four grammatical sentences using the words correctly deserve full marks.
questions.explanation: Vocabulary recall plus active use in simple sentences.

questions.question: Describe the geography of the Himalaya as given in the chapter: its extent, its protective and rain-making role, its great rivers with their sources, and its principal peaks.
questions.answer: The Himalayan chain runs roughly 2,400 kilometres across the north of the Indian subcontinent, standing like a sentinel (प्रहरीव) at the head of the land. Its protective role is twofold: it wards off the freezing northern winds, and it blocks the monsoon clouds so that they shed their rain over India — which is why the plains remain सस्यश्यामला, green with crops. It is the mother of the great rivers: the Ganga rises from the Gangotri glacier at Gomukh and first flows as the Bhagirathi; the Yamuna rises at Yamunotri; the Brahmaputra and the Sindhu are also born in the Himalayan and trans-Himalayan region. These rivers water the fields and sustain crores of people, and are revered as mothers. Of its peaks, Everest (Sagarmatha, in Nepal) is the highest summit on earth, while Kanchenjunga is the highest peak within India. Kalidasa's picture of the range dipping into the eastern and western oceans (पूर्वापरौ तोयनिधी) is poetic geography expressing this ocean-to-ocean breadth.
questions.explanation: Extent, protection, rains, rivers with sources, and peaks — all five elements.

questions.question: 'हिमालयः तपोभूमिः तीर्थभूमिश्च' — write an essay on the spiritual and natural significance of the Himalaya: its shrines, its role as the land of tapas, and its forests and wildlife.
questions.answer: The Himalaya is at once India's sanctuary of nature and its sanctuary of the spirit. As तीर्थभूमि it bears the four dhams — Gangotri and Yamunotri at the sources of the two sister rivers, Kedarnath the seat of Shiva, and Badrinath the seat of Vishnu. In the Amarnath cave pilgrims behold a linga formed of ice (हिममयं शिवलिङ्गम्), and beyond the main range rise Kailash and Lake Mansarovar, the goal of the hardiest yatris. As तपोभूमि it was the chosen ground of the rishis: its solitude, purity and stillness made it the natural home of meditation, and epic and kavya alike picture hermitages on its slopes — the Kumarasambhava itself shows Parvati performing tapas there. Its natural wealth completes the picture: forests of deodar (देवदारु, 'wood of the gods') and birch; great medicinal herbs (महौषधयः); and rare creatures — the musk deer with its fragrant kasturi, the snow leopard, the monal — with wonders like Uttarakhand's Valley of Flowers. Nature and spirit are not separate here: it is precisely the mountain's grandeur and purity that made it sacred. That is why the poets call the divine-souled mountain the crown of India.
questions.explanation: Shrines, tapas tradition, flora-fauna — and their unity — in essay form.

questions.question: Take the epithets and key words of Kumarasambhava 1.1 — हिमालयः, नगाधिराजः, देवतात्मा, तोयनिधी, पूर्वापरौ, मानदण्डः — and for each give the विग्रह and the name of the समास. Also identify the कृदन्त forms in the verse.
questions.answer: समास: (1) हिमालयः = हिमस्य आलयः 'abode of snow' — षष्ठी-तत्पुरुषः. (2) नगाधिराजः = नगानाम् अधिराजः 'overlord of mountains' — षष्ठी-तत्पुरुषः. (3) देवतात्मा = देवता आत्मा यस्य सः 'whose self is divine' — बहुव्रीहिः (it denotes the possessor, the Himalaya, not its own members). (4) तोयनिधी = तोयानां निधी 'treasuries of water' (the two oceans) — षष्ठी-तत्पुरुषः in the dual. (5) पूर्वापरौ = पूर्वश्च अपरश्च 'the eastern and the western' — द्वन्द्वः. (6) मानदण्डः = मानस्य दण्डः 'rod of measuring' — षष्ठी-तत्पुरुषः. कृदन्त forms: अवगाह्य (वगाह्य) — the ल्यप् gerund 'having plunged into', used because the root गाह् carries the prefix अव; and स्थितः — the क्त past participle of स्था, 'standing', agreeing with नगाधिराजः in gender, number and case.
questions.explanation: A complete grammatical anatomy of the verse's compounds and kridantas.

questions.question: Translate the following passage into English: 'हिमालयः भारतस्य उत्तरस्यां दिशि प्रहरीव तिष्ठति। सः शीतलान् उत्तरवातान् निवारयति, मेघान् च अवरुध्य वृष्टिं कारयति। अस्मात् नगाधिराजात् गङ्गा यमुना इत्यादयः महानद्यः प्रभवन्ति। ऋषयः पुरा हिमालये एव तपः आचरन्। अतः कवयः तं भारतस्य मुकुटम् इति वदन्ति।'
questions.answer: Translation: The Himalaya stands like a sentinel in the northern direction of India. It wards off the cold northern winds and, blocking the clouds, causes the rain to fall. From this king of mountains rise the great rivers — the Ganga, the Yamuna and others. In ancient times the sages performed their tapas (austerity) in the Himalaya itself. Therefore the poets call it the crown of India.
questions.explanation: Key constructions: प्रहरीव 'like a sentinel'; अवरुध्य gerund 'having blocked'; अस्मात् नगाधिराजात् ablative 'from this king of mountains'; आचरन् imperfect 'they performed'.

questions.question: Read the passage and answer: 'The Kumarasambhava is a mahakavya of Kalidasa. Its subject is the marriage of Shiva and Parvati and the events leading to the birth of their son Kumara (Kartikeya). Parvati is the daughter of the Himalaya, and so the poem opens with a portrait of the mountain: अस्त्युत्तरस्यां दिशि देवतात्मा हिमालयो नाम नगाधिराजः।' — (a) Who is Kumara? (b) Why does the poem open with the Himalaya? (c) What does नगाधिराजः mean?
questions.answer: (a) Kumara is Kartikeya, the son of Shiva and Parvati, whose birth gives the poem its name (कुमारसम्भवम् = 'the birth of Kumara'). (b) Because Parvati, the heroine, is the daughter of the Himalaya — the poem begins by introducing her father, the mountain. (c) नगाधिराजः means 'the overlord/king of mountains' (नगानाम् अधिराजः).
questions.explanation: Comprehension of the poem's frame: hero's birth, heroine's father, and the epithet.

questions.question: Read the verse and answer: 'अस्त्युत्तरस्यां दिशि देवतात्मा हिमालयो नाम नगाधिराजः। पूर्वापरौ तोयनिधी वगाह्य स्थितः पृथिव्या इव मानदण्डः॥' — (a) In which direction does the Himalaya stand? (b) Into what does it plunge (तोयनिधी)? (c) To what is it compared, and by which word?
questions.answer: (a) In the northern direction (उत्तरस्यां दिशि). (b) Into the two oceans — the eastern and the western (पूर्वापरौ तोयनिधी, 'the two treasuries of water'). (c) It is compared to the measuring rod of the earth (पृथिव्याः मानदण्डः), with the comparison word इव ('like').
questions.explanation: Direct comprehension of the three limbs of the verse.

questions.question: Read the verse and answer: 'अनन्तरत्नप्रभवस्य यस्य हिमं न सौभाग्यविलोपि जातम्। एको हि दोषो गुणसन्निपाते निमज्जतीन्दोः किरणेष्विवाङ्कः॥' (कुमारसम्भवम् 1.3) — (a) What possible 'flaw' of the Himalaya is being discussed? (b) What general truth does the poet state? (c) What simile illustrates it?
questions.answer: (a) The endless snow (हिमम्) — one might object that perpetual cold and snow is a defect in the mountain. (b) The general truth: a single fault sinks unnoticed where virtues are gathered in a heap (एको हि दोषो गुणसन्निपाते निमज्जति) — the Himalaya, source of countless gems, loses none of its splendour for its snow. (c) The simile of the moon: the dark spot (अङ्कः) of the moon disappears in the beauty of its rays (इन्दोः किरणेषु इव).
questions.explanation: Verse 1.3: objection, general truth (arthantaranyasa) and the moon simile.

questions.question: Read the passage and answer: 'हिमालयः भारतस्य उत्तरस्यां दिशि प्रहरीव तिष्ठति। सः शीतलान् उत्तरवातान् निवारयति, मेघान् च अवरुध्य वृष्टिं कारयति। अतः एव भारतभूमिः सस्यश्यामला वर्तते।' — (a) Like what does the Himalaya stand? (b) What two services does it perform? (c) What is the result for the land of India?
questions.answer: (a) Like a sentinel/watchman (प्रहरीव). (b) It wards off the cold northern winds (शीतलान् उत्तरवातान् निवारयति) and, blocking the clouds, causes the rains (मेघान् अवरुध्य वृष्टिं कारयति). (c) As a result the land of India remains green with crops — सस्यश्यामला.
questions.explanation: Comprehension of the prose on the mountain's protective role.

questions.question: Read the passage and answer: 'अस्मात् नगाधिराजात् गङ्गा यमुना ब्रह्मपुत्रः सिन्धुः इत्यादयः महानद्यः प्रभवन्ति। गङ्गा गङ्गोत्रीहिमानीतः गोमुखात् भागीरथीरूपेण निःसरति, यमुना च यमुनोत्रीतः। एताः नद्यः कोटिशः जनान् जीवयन्ति।' — (a) Which rivers are named? (b) From where and in what form does the Ganga issue? (c) Why are these rivers so important?
questions.answer: (a) The Ganga, the Yamuna, the Brahmaputra and the Sindhu (Indus). (b) The Ganga issues from the Gangotri glacier (गङ्गोत्रीहिमानी) at Gomukh, in the form of the Bhagirathi (भागीरथीरूपेण). (c) Because they give life to crores of people (कोटिशः जनान् जीवयन्ति) — watering the fields and sustaining the plains.
questions.explanation: Comprehension of the prose on the Himalayan rivers.

questions.question: Read the passage and answer: 'हिमालयस्य वनेषु देवदारुभूर्जादयः वृक्षाः शोभन्ते, महौषधयश्च प्रभवन्ति। तत्र कस्तूरीमृगः हिमचित्रकः मोनाल-पक्षी च निवसन्ति। उत्तराखण्डे पुष्पघाटी इति प्रसिद्धा उपत्यका वर्तते।' — (a) Which trees adorn the Himalayan forests? (b) Which three creatures are named? (c) What famous valley is mentioned, and where?
questions.answer: (a) The deodar (देवदारु), the birch (भूर्ज) and other such trees — along with great medicinal herbs (महौषधयः). (b) The musk deer (कस्तूरीमृगः), the snow leopard (हिमचित्रकः) and the monal bird. (c) The Valley of Flowers (पुष्पघाटी), in Uttarakhand.
questions.explanation: Comprehension of the prose on Himalayan flora and fauna.

questions.question: Read and answer: 'ऋषयः मुनयश्च पुरा हिमालये एव तपः आचरन्। अतः कवयः तं भारतस्य मुकुटम् इति वदन्ति। गीतायाम् अपि उक्तम् — स्थावराणां हिमालयः इति।' — (a) What did the rishis do in the Himalaya? (b) What do the poets call the mountain, and why is the metaphor apt? (c) What does the Gita quotation assert?
questions.answer: (a) In ancient times the rishis and munis performed their tapas (austerity/meditation) in the Himalaya itself. (b) The poets call it the crown of India (भारतस्य मुकुटम्); the metaphor is apt because a crown sits at the head (the mountain crowns India's north), gleams with jewels (snows, gems, herbs) and marks sovereignty (it is the king of mountains). (c) That among immovable things the Lord himself is the Himalaya — the mountain is counted among the divine glories (विभूति).
questions.explanation: Comprehension plus evaluation of the crown metaphor and the Gita reference.

questions.question: Grammar case study. Consider the words of the verse: अस्त्युत्तरस्यां, हिमालयः, देवतात्मा, अवगाह्य, स्थितः. — (a) Split अस्त्युत्तरस्यां and name the sandhi. (b) Which of the listed words is a बहुव्रीहि compound, and what is its विग्रह? (c) Identify the two कृदन्त forms and name their suffixes.
questions.answer: (a) अस्त्युत्तरस्यां = अस्ति + उत्तरस्याम् — यण्-सन्धिः (इ before उ becomes य्). (b) देवतात्मा — विग्रह: देवता आत्मा यस्य सः, 'he whose self is divine'; it denotes the possessor (the Himalaya), hence बहुव्रीहि. (c) अवगाह्य — the gerund in ल्यप् ('having plunged into', prefixed root अव + गाह्); स्थितः — the past participle in क्त (स्था + क्त = 'standing').
questions.explanation: One integrated grammar drill: sandhi, samasa and kridanta from a single verse.

questions.question: Read the passage and answer in English: 'हिमालयः तपोभूमिः अस्ति। तत्र शीतलः वायुः वहति, निर्मलाः नद्यः प्रवहन्ति, उच्चानि शिखराणि हिमेन आच्छादितानि सन्ति। पर्यटकाः तीर्थयात्रिकाश्च प्रतिवर्षं तत्र गच्छन्ति।' — (a) Translate the passage. (b) Which word tells us the peaks are 'covered with snow'? (c) Who goes there every year?
questions.answer: (a) Translation: The Himalaya is a land of tapas (austerity). There a cool wind blows, clear rivers flow, and the high peaks are covered with snow. Tourists and pilgrims go there every year. (b) आच्छादितानि ('covered'), with हिमेन ('with snow') — हिमेन आच्छादितानि = covered with snow. (c) Tourists (पर्यटकाः) and pilgrims (तीर्थयात्रिकाः) go there every year (प्रतिवर्षम्).
questions.explanation: Straightforward prose translation with two targeted word questions.

questions.question: Read the two statements and answer: (i) Kalidasa: 'पूर्वापरौ तोयनिधी वगाह्य स्थितः पृथिव्या इव मानदण्डः' — the Himalaya dips into the eastern and western oceans. (ii) Geography: the Himalayan range runs about 2,400 km across the north but does not literally touch either sea. — (a) Translate statement (i). (b) Do the two statements contradict each other? Explain how a reader of kavya should reconcile them.
questions.answer: (a) Translation: 'Plunging into the eastern and the western oceans, (the Himalaya) stands like the measuring rod of the earth.' (b) There is no real contradiction. Kalidasa writes poetry, not a survey report: the ocean-to-ocean image is poetic geography (a poet's convention) expressing the range's enormous east-west sweep across the whole breadth of the land. The reader should take from it the suggestion of immensity that serves the मानदण्ड simile — only a rod spanning sea to sea could 'measure' the earth — while the 2,400 km figure remains the literal fact.
questions.explanation: Distinguishing poetic truth (kavya) from literal geographic fact.
